collection.description: Early one morning, a villager spots a canoe coming in from the north, low in the water and patched with bark.

ask.text:
Early one morning, (name) spots a canoe coming in from the north, low in the water and patched with bark. As it gets closer, (he/she) can see a family aboard: tired, sunburnt, sitting very close together.
They land on the beach and don't come any further. One of them stands up and explains, in a voice hoarse from the sea, that their island had a terrible year: the fish left and the gardens failed. They ask, very politely, whether there's anywhere they could rest a few days before going on.
The village is not rich this season, and some people are already muttering about the food. What should (name) do?

choices.label: Give Them Supplies for the Journey

text_only.reason: the word in the owner's story; what changes in the game is the ending's own EFFECT line (the ledger), so this word alone changes nothing

c1o1.text: Under a sail cloth at the bottom of the canoe there's a baby, fast asleep, the reason they sat so close. Two days of rest becomes a week, and then one of them is fixing roof thatch without being asked and the other is out with the fishers, and by the end of the month nobody remembers deciding they should stay. {#made:Only one of them can, as the village has no room for more|Only two of them can, as the village has no room for more|They just did}. The baby learns to walk on the village path, holding onto (name)'s fingers.

c1o2.text: There are three of them: a grandparent with arms like rope from years of paddling, a gangly teen who won't stop staring at the village's huts, and a small child who falls asleep in the first warm lap (he/she) can find. The grandparent takes one look at the gardens and starts telling the farmers what they're doing wrong. Annoyingly, the grandparent is right. {#made:Only one of them can stay; the village has no room for more|Only two of them can stay; the village has no room for more|They decide to stay}.

c1.text: (Name) walks down the beach and holds out (his/her) hand. "You won't rest on the sand," (he/she) says. "Come up to the fire." Behind (him/her), a few of the mutterers go quiet...

c2o1.text: They load the food carefully, and push off on the evening tide, and wave until they're just a dot on the water. (Name) stands on the beach long after they've gone. The food store is a little emptier. For weeks, (name) finds (himself/herself) looking north in the mornings, wondering if they ever found where they were going.

c2o2.text: The baby, hidden under the sail cloth until now, starts to cry just as they're pushing off. And something about the sound reaches the whole village at once. The people who were muttering are the first ones down the beach, waving their arms. "Wait. Come back. There's room." {#made:There is, but only for one of them, who stays|There is, but only for two of them, who stay|There is, and they decide to stay}.

c2.text: (Name) fetches dried fish, water gourds and a basket of fruit and carries it down to the canoe. The family thanks (him/her) over and over...
